message.content: Repo /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper. ADR 0026 slice S7b (trail #317; read `entire trail show 317 --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper --project gh/orin-dx`, and trail #259's checklist, docs/adr/0026-the-checker-is-the-type-authority.md section S7 and 'Gates before the default flips', docs/type-checker-integration.md). Branch from origin/main as `feat/fallback-off-mode`. Context: S8 made the checker the default (`--no-checker` selects the structural resolver); the process route is gone (#445 pending); the structural resolver still runs as the fallback for anything the checker cannot answer and as the first answer in the addon. S7 will delete the resolver for what the construct suite covers; S7b is the gate that proves it: 'every suite row passes with the fallback off'. Deliver: (1) A way to run Caliper with the structural FALLBACK OFF for rows the checker answers (internal switch used by the suite/lane: prefer one existing mechanism (an existing PipelineOptions/semantic request field or hidden flag) over a new public option; ADR/`docs` must say it is internal; no new user-facing option unless unavoidable): when on, a prop/type the checker cannot answer is reported as a typed `degradedBy` unknown/diagnostic (never a silently structural answer), so the lane shows exactly which rows still depend on the fallback. (2) A 'no-checker' construct lane or the lane's fallback-off column in `just test-checker-lane` (apps/oracle construct-suite; expectations files; keep `construct:parity` untouched): list per row whether it passes with fallback off; the result is the exact worklist for S7c-S7e (rows that still need the structural path, grouped by cause). (3) New suite rows for the constructs the structural path covers that the suite does not (check the 'Unsolved' and fallback gap notes in ADR 0026 and docs/rdt-differences.md; add rows where a real component pattern would break when the resolver is deleted: e.g. hooks/lowercase helpers excluded by the universe, `default`-keyed exports, lib-parameter functions: see spectrum gap notes; each new row has the expected checker answer from the real checker, goldens captured with the Go checker via `construct:capture`, checked with tsrs via `construct:parity`). Do not delete any resolver code in this slice. Report the worklist: row count that pass with fallback off vs depend on fallback, by cause. Constraints: crates/semantic/src/{rpc,checker,on_demand}.rs are owned by open PRs (#445, #449, #451): do not edit them; keep core/semantic hunks small and merge origin/main before the final push. Rust 1.99.1 toolchain first on PATH (/Users/gabe/.rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin; commits need MISE_RUST_VERSION=1.99.1), own CARGO_TARGET_DIR under ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/s7b/ (no /tmp), outside the sandbox where tests need it, `pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile` if needed. Free gates only (construct:capture/check/parity are free); NO oracle runs (`scripts/weekly.py --oracle`), no corpus fetches, no new scripts/recipes unless a CI job calls them. Output of normal `extract` must stay byte-identical (diff on ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large/src and ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/checker-default/chakra-only/src). Tests fail-on-base. Changeset as fits; update ADR 0026 S7b marker and the trail checklist text in docs only (do not edit trails). Before push: `just lint doc-check machete typos`, `just deny`, `just semver`, `just test-rust`, `just test-checker-lane`, `just test-ts`; judge by exit code. Signed commits with trailer `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ`; `git push origin HEAD:feat/fallback-off-mode` (never --no-verify), verify with `git ls-remote`. Do not open the PR, do not poll CI. Final report <= 300 words: the mechanism, the worklist (counts by cause), new rows, SHAs, what was not verified.

Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.
</system-reminder>

Description:
Goal
Make the checker the default type authority, with oxc supplying syntax (the opt-in decision of ADR 0006 and 0007 is superseded). ADR 0026 (accepted) records the decision, the fallback and degradedBy rules, the version pin policy and distribution. The checker is tsrs, linked in process through the published tsrs_api and tsrs_vfs crates (trail #369); the Go typescript@7.1.0-beta stays only as the oracle, the construct-suite goldens and the tsrs-vs-Go parity gate in apps/oracle.
Slice checklist (ADR 0026)
[x] S1 projection model and PropType variants
[x] S2 converter and memo
[x] S3 React terminals by declaring path
[x] S4 the checker's answer wins (addon within the ADR 0022 window, CLI waiting)
[x] S5 generic and polymorphic components through a virtual file
[x] S6 watch with updateSnapshot and stale-file stamps
[x] S7a oxc supplies the syntax facts; S7a2 defaults and union order (#326, #435)
[ ] S7b a fallback-off mode, a no-checker lane and new suite rows (#317)
[ ] S7c a thin structural fallback, scoped to syntax only (#318)
[ ] S7d dependency type loading becomes checker-only (#319)
[ ] S7e delete the resolver modules and the extractor's declaration walk (#320); this also gates the lighter semantic IR (see the IR spike)
[x] S7f dropped with Windows (trail #370)
[x] S8 the checker is the default, --no-checker selects the structural resolver (#441)
Done around the slices
In-process crates (#369: #438 transport, #440 guards, #445 delete the process route), extract speed against RDT (#443, #444 follow-up pending a re-merge, #446, #447, #448, #449 under trail #382), weekly records the checker (#442, trail #351), startup prefetch (#432), condition-map memo (#430), degraded fallback (#437), drop Windows (#436), ADR 0027 accepted (#450).
Remaining
S7b to S7e; the Storybook live upgrade of a structural answer to the checker's; the oracle run against the checker default; the accuracy follow-ups (the 5 less precise construct rows, single-line JSDoc, ReactElement to ReactNode mapping, #328, #298).
Rule
Link every new branch to this trail or to its slice trail, so the PRs keep their feature meaning.

5	## Context
6	
7	ADR 0006 and 0007 made the TypeScript checker an opt-in second resolver, because a whole-project `tsc` run cost up to 9.3 s and 975 MiB (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`); ADR 0022 bounded it to a warm per-component request. A prototype found more: `[string, ...number[]]` prints as `[string, number[][]]` and a getter reads as a method. Each fix is another rule in a resolver that re-implements the type system.
8	
9	tsrs (`oxc-project/tsrs`, Apache-2.0) is a Rust port of the TypeScript 7 checker at microsoft/TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`, the commit `typescript@7.1.0-beta` was built from. It speaks the same `--api` protocol: the 19 methods caliper calls are all present, and 87 one-prop fixtures got the same oracle verdicts as `typescript-beta`. 10	
11	## Decision
12	
13	The checker decides types and oxc decides syntax.
14	
15	- **Authority.** The checker is the default source of a component's prop set, each prop's type, requiredness and description. oxc supplies candidate components (`extractor/evidence.rs`, `uses.rs`), defaults, JSDoc positions, source locations and declaration order, which is re-applied to union members because the checker sorts them by flags and value.
16	- **One projection model.** Checker facts convert once into the canonical model. Canonical JSON, TOON and the RDT view are projections of it, and no projection makes a type decision.
17	- **Fallback.** The structural resolver stays only for when the checker cannot answer: not installed or offline, an unsupported platform, a crash, a timeout. Its types carry `degradedBy` and the run carries one diagnostic.
18	- **Opt-out.** The checker runs unless `--no-checker` (`checker: false` in the config, the napi binding and the Storybook addon) turns it off; `--experimental-semantic-types` and `semanticTypes` are removed (S8).
19	- **Per surface.** The Storybook addon keeps ADR 0022: the structural answer first, the checker's within `semanticWaitMs`. Its premise that the checker is too slow for first paint was re-measured with tsrs in S4 and holds (Chakra's `Button`, 562 ms, 402 ms after the first-answer work). The CLI and agents wait for the checker, all candidates in one snapshot, with a timeout (10 s proposed).
20	- **Pin.** We pin exact tsrs crates (`tsrs_api` and `tsrs_vfs` `=0.24.0`, TypeScript `3e9236361fa9`) and bump them on purpose, never through dependabot (its ignore list); the npm `tsrs` the parity gate runs (`apps/oracle`, `0.24.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, the same TypeScript commit) moves with them, and `scripts/check-packaging.mjs` fails while the two name different releases. A bump passes the deterministic construct suite (`apps/oracle/construct-suite`, being built on `feat/construct-suite`) and a tsrs-against-Go parity run of it. The weekly oracle keeps the Go `typescript` checker: an oracle running the checker that produced the answer agrees with it by construction.
21	- **Linked.** The product links the tsrs crates and asks `tsrs_api::Session` in process, on one thread with a 512 MiB stack, the stack the `tsrs` binary serves on; nothing is installed, and there is no other checker to choose. The Go `typescript` beta is the oracle, the construct goldens and the parity gate, in `apps/oracle` only. The linked checker is never replaced, since a fresh session raises this process's memory rather than returning it; past `OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib`, read from its own arenas, it stops for the session and components keep their structural answer with a diagnostic. A panic closes its session and a fresh one answers the next request, and a file nested past 20,000 brackets is not given to it (trail 369 slice 2).
22	- **Collapsed React types.** `ReactElement`, `JSX.Element` and `ReactChild` stay collapsed to the `reactNode` terminal. No evaluation showed it hurting Storybook controls.
23	
24	Linked rather than spawned (trail 369): the crates are published (0.24.0), the same recorded Chakra answer (3,776 requests) takes 141 ms in process against 367 ms over the pipe with equal answers, and there is no per-platform binary to ship or find. 25	
26	Trail 369 slice 4 (done, 2026-11-12) deleted the product's process route: `--tsc-path` and `tscPath` (CLI, config, napi, Storybook addon), `crates/tsc-client`, the binary lookup and the version allow-list it checked, and the replay tests that ran recordings of the Go checker through a fake `tsc` process; those tests ask the linked checker now. Slice 5's pin rule is in **Pin** above. Spawning a binary stays rejected (Alternatives).
27	
28	## Consequences
29	
30	- Supersedes "structural stays the default" in ADR 0006 and 0007 and 0007's "never a silent default" trigger. The rest of both stands.
31	- Deletable or shrinkable with a thin fallback, estimated from each file's header: in `crates/core/src/resolver`, `alias`, `chain`, `evaluate`, `substitute`, `named`, `primitives`, `extends`, `func`, `template`, `import`, `callee`, `memo`, `deps`, `collected` and `precedence` shrink to a no-generics subset and `mod.rs` by half; `dependency_types.rs` and `import_map.rs` go (the checker resolves modules; ADR 0010 and 0025 narrow to the fallback); in `extractor`, `interface` (but cva), `alias`, `values`, `reexports`, `asserted` and most of `visit` go, and `component`, `wrapper` and `mod.rs` shrink to candidate detection. 33	- No cache is keyed on a type id: ids are per checker and change with query order. Keys are file content, export name, instantiation and the tsrs pin. The checker does not see an edit it is not told about, so watch forwards every change.
34	- Unsolved: a per-component dependency closure from the checker (invalidation stays conservative), and the structural answer's gaps wherever the fallback runs.
35	- Risks: tsrs is pre-1.0, four releases in twelve days, and closed to pull requests (its README). 36	
37	Migration, each slice behind a deterministic gate, none on the oracle. The tsrs backend (the Rust client running on tsrs, PR 390) is done.
38	
39	1. **S1** (done) Shared projection model and the new `PropType` variants, filled by the structural path where it knows them. Gate: a unit test per variant, golden JSON diff, cache schema test.
40	2. **S2** (done) Flag-based converter in `convert.rs`, memoized by type id within one snapshot, with a named-boundary policy and caps. Gate: the construct suite's expected JSON; reversed query order gives identical bytes.
41	3. **S3** (done) React terminals by declaring path. Gate: no regression against today's Chakra `Button` terminals.

44	6. **S6** (done, one gate failed) Watch on `snapshot.update` with RSS recycling: the warm checker keeps its snapshot and brings it up to date with `updateSnapshot` (`ensurePrograms`, the files the session announced), and before an answer compares every file its program read with the stamp it had; an unannounced change answers from a fresh snapshot with a warning naming the file ([watch](../type-checker-integration.md#watch-adr-0026-slice-s6)). 49	
50	S8 stays behind these gates (status at the flip, 2026-11-12):
51	
52	- The checker lane of the construct suite (caliper's checker path over `apps/oracle/construct-suite`) shows no regression against the structural path except listed improvements. **PASS**: `just test-checker-lane` on the S8 branch.

57	
58	The determinism and memory gates are measured by `just gate-measure`, on the linked checker since trail 369 slice 2 (both PASS in process); what it reads, and why the first gate's wording cannot be met as written (tsrs's `--api` has no checker-count option), is in [gate measurements](../gate-measurements.md). 59	
60	## Alternatives considered
61	
62	- **Keep the checker opt-in.** Two sources of truth, and the default keeps the silent wrong answers above.
63	- **Checker for the addon only.** The CLI and agents read the same wrong types, and they can afford to wait.
64	- **Spawn the `tsrs` binary** (`@tsrs/<platform>` with the npm packages). 65	- **Parse with `tsrs_parser` instead of oxc.** Unpublished like every tsrs crate, and the extractor is written against oxc's AST, which already gives the syntactic facts kept here at about 2 ms per incremental update.
66	- **Keep investing in the structural resolver.** Each defect class above re-implements a checker rule and was silent until a comparison found it.

- The checker lane of the construct suite (caliper's checker path over `apps/oracle/construct-suite`) shows no regression against the structural path except listed improvements. **PASS**: `just test-checker-lane` on the S8 branch.

For the linked checker the memory gate's threshold is the same 768 MiB read from its arenas, and crossing it stops the checker rather than recycling it.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep the checker opt-in.** Two sources of truth, and the default keeps the silent wrong answers above.
- **Checker for the addon only.** The CLI and agents read the same wrong types, and they can afford to wait.
- **Spawn the `tsrs` binary** (`@tsrs/<platform>` with the npm packages). Process isolation and a restart lever, but the pipe costs more than the checker (367 against 141 ms on one answer), and every platform needs a binary found or shipped. Rejected; the route that ran one (`--tsc-path`) was deleted in trail 369 slice 4.
- **Parse with `tsrs_parser` instead of oxc.** Unpublished like every tsrs crate, and the extractor is written against oxc's AST, which already gives the syntactic facts kept here at about 2 ms per incremental update.
- **Keep investing in the structural resolver.** Each defect class above re-implements a checker rule and was silent until a comparison found it.

117	## The algorithm
118	
119	Mirrors RDT 2.4.0 (`lib/parser.js`). Method names are from the 7.1 client.
120	
121	1. `getSymbolOfSourceFile(file)`, then `getExportsOfModule`.
122	2. For each export, `getTypeOfSymbol`, then `getSignaturesOfType(Call)`. A component has a signature whose first parameter is named `props` or is the only parameter. For a class, use `Construct` signatures and read `props` from the instance type.
123	3. Props type: `getTypeOfSymbolAtLocation(param, param.valueDeclaration)`. Props: the type's apparent properties, plus each member's when it is a union.
124	4. Per prop, `type` is `typeToString(getBaseConstraintOfType(t) ?? t)` with default flags, so long types truncate as they do in RDT. `required` means the symbol lacks `Optional` and has no code default.
125	5. `parent` is the first declaration's parent when that is an interface or type alias. `declarations` is every declaration's parent.
126	6. `description` and `tags` come from `getDocumentationComment` and `getJsDocTags`.
127	
128	RDT also emits any exported symbol that has a JSDoc comment but no props. We don't. In the fixture corpus, 23 of the 26 entries only RDT emits are of this kind, such as enum members, type aliases and functions.

130	### The converter (ADR 0026, slice S2)
131	
132	A prop's checker type becomes a `PropType` from structured answers only (`crates/semantic/src/convert.rs`): the type flags, a union's members (`getTypesOfType`), a reference's arguments, a tuple type's element flags (`getTargetOfType`), an object's signatures, properties and index signatures (one `batchRequests`), and an alias's symbol and arguments. `typeToString` is used for a name to display, and for two facts the API does not state: which parameter is optional and what a tuple element is labeled (`printed.rs` reads them from the printed type and refuses text that does not read to its end; a fact it cannot read is never replaced by a guess).
133	
134	- **Named boundary.** An interface or class declared under `node_modules` or in the TypeScript lib (`Date`, `Promise<T>`, `HTMLElement`), and an object type a dependency's alias names, stay `named` with their arguments. A function type is always expanded. The lib's utilities (`Partial`, `Pick`, `Omit`, `Record`) are expanded: their result is the type. A dependency's union of literals is expanded, since its members are the values a control offers. React's `ReactNode`, `ElementType`, `CSSProperties` and `ReactElement` are recognized by where they are declared.
135	- **Caps.** Depth 5, 500 members at the top and 120 below it (a union, an intersection, a tuple's elements), and a budget of 100 properties at the top and 40 below it that counts only the members the project did not declare (inherited from a dependency or the lib, or with no declaration). A cut type is `truncated` with the limit (and, for a width, the total), which `degradedBy` reports. Every descent into the parts of a type (an object, union, intersection, array, tuple or template literal) passes one gate (`Converter::enter`) that checks, before anything is fetched, whether the type encloses itself or is too deep; the width is checked after it, where the type is known. A test has a prop for each cap.
136	- **Wide object types.** What the project declares is listed whole however wide: an interface of 150 own fields is never cut. Over the budget of members from outside the project, the rest stands as what it is named through, and the project's own members stay beside it. A utility wrapper (`Omit`, `Pick`, `Partial`, `Required`, `Readonly`) is kept as `named` with its arguments when what it applies to has a name of its own: a React DOM attribute type becomes `htmlAttributes` (recognized by the declaring file `/@types/react/` and the interface's name, with the element read from its type argument by the same table the structural path uses, `HTMLAnchorElement` is `a`; an element the table does not know is not guessed), and another dependency or lib type is a `named` layer. The checker keeps no `ComponentPropsWithoutRef`, only the `Omit<..., "ref">` it expands to, which is kept as written. Under the budget the wrapper is expanded (`Pick<ComponentProps<"button">, "disabled" | "type">` has two props). A class or interface of the project that extends such types (`interface BoxProps extends Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "color">`) is an intersection of its own fields and each base type (`getBaseTypes`), a base of the project seen through to its own bases; an instantiation of a generic one, as the type itself or as one base among others, states no bases in terms of its arguments, so the type is cut: its members from outside are `truncated` with their real count beside its own, and the other bases are not named in its place. A type that is not wrapped (`HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>` as a prop) is the `named` it always was.
137	- **React aliases flattened into a union.** The checker flattens `ReactNode | Fn` into the members of `ReactNode`, so a union that holds all of them (`ReactElement`, `ReactPortal` and an `Iterable` of `ReactNode`, found by declaration, with the primitives) is `reactNode` again beside the rest of its members. `ElementType` below the top of a prop arrives the same way and is wider than the budget: it is recognized (more than 100 of React's own tag names, a fixed table of `JSX.IntrinsicElements`, with `ComponentClass` and `FunctionComponent`) and kept as the terminal instead of cut, and only those tag names go into it: any other string literal the author wrote beside it (`ElementType | "custom-widget"`) stays a member of the union, as does a tag a project adds to `JSX.IntrinsicElements`; narrower, it is listed. `ReactElement`, `JSX.Element` and `ReactChild` stay collapsed to `reactNode` (ADR 0026).
138	- **Recursion** is a `recursive` marker named by the declaration (the alias or interface) with the instantiation's type arguments. Whether a type is one it is inside of is decided by its type handle, which is the instantiation: `Box<string>` inside `Box<Box<string>>` is another type from the one around it and is expanded, while `Tree<string>` inside `Tree<string>` is a back-reference; an alias of an array or tuple of itself (`type Loop = Loop[]`) ends at the first lap. A handle is only compared inside one conversion, never stored in an answer; type handles change with the order of queries, so a test asks last to first and compares bytes. The per-snapshot memo is keyed by the handle, the depth and the set of enclosing handles, so a hit gives what a miss would.
139	- **Union order.** The checker sorts a union's members by kind and value. The merge puts them back in the order the declaration writes them, read by oxc (see "Defaults and union order" below), and where that does not place every member, in the structural union's order (`types/semantic/order.rs`): a member is found by equality, `boolean` by a boolean literal, a named type by its name without the namespace it was written through (`React.Ref` is `Ref`), and a union the structural pass keeps as string values (`literalUnion`) gives their order. Members the structural union lacks (an `undefined` it dropped, a type it left named) follow the ones it has, in the checker's order. A union neither orders keeps the checker's order, with no marker.
140	- **Debug stat.** With `RUST_LOG=caliper_docgen_semantic=debug`, each component logs its request count and milliseconds, and the session logs requests by method and memo hits.

142	### Condition maps
143	
144	A dependency's condition map is one mapped type instantiated many times over one set of keys: Chakra's `ConditionalValue<V>` is `V | Array<V | null> | { [K in keyof Conditions]?: ConditionalValue<V> }`, and a `Button`'s props hold 538 of them, one per value type, all over `Conditions`' 130 keys. Each is wider than the budget below a prop and is cut, which reads two things of its list of properties: how many there are, and whether the project declared any. Listing them took 31.5 MB and 447 ms one map at a time; the constraint's members take one request of 1.3 ms, which the parts cache keeps.
145	
146	The converter keeps, per snapshot, the count of a map by `(the handle of its constraint, the symbol that declares it)` (`State::maps` in `crates/semantic/src/convert.rs`), and cuts a later map of the same key without asking for its properties. A map is reused only when all of these hold:
147	
148	- it is no alias's (a named `Partial<A>` has the type it applies to, which the key does not hold) and has no `as` clause, which would rename the keys;
149	- the list its count came from had no property the project declares, no signature and no index signature;
150	- its declaration's keys hold no type parameter, so its properties are declared in the same places whatever it is instantiated with (below, "Who declares the properties");
151	- the count is over the budget where the later map sits (40 below a prop, 100 at the top). A map that fits is converted from its own properties' symbols and types, which another map's list does not give, so it asks for them.
152	
153	**When reuse is exact.** A mapped type without an `as` clause has one property per literal key of its constraint, whatever its template, and a handle is one type inside a snapshot, so two maps of one constraint handle have the same keys and as many properties; a mapped type has no signatures, and a counted list with no index signature has a constraint with no `string` or `number`. A cut reads only the count, whether a property is the project's, and the signatures and index signatures (none): what two such maps differ in, each property's type and optionality, it does not read, and the printed text it keeps (`{ c01?: string | undefined; … }`) is asked of each map. The cut is then the same as from the map's own list, and so is everything the conversion above it recorded: the gate, the `asked` set and the enclosing instantiations it compared are unchanged, because no instantiation is looked at between the gate and the cut, and the parts cache is not touched. The entry lives in the snapshot's converter, so a new snapshot starts with none, as the handles it is keyed by do.
154	
155	**Who declares the properties.** The 7.1 API cannot be asked which type a map is homomorphic over (it has no `getModifiersTypeOfMappedType`), and a key of one constraint handle and one symbol does not say: `type Picked<T, K extends keyof T> = null | { [P in K]?: T[P] }` over the same written-out keys, given a dependency's interface and then the project's, is one key, and the properties of each are declared where its `T`'s are. So a count is kept only for a map whose declaration's constraint holds no type parameter: the declared type's (`getTargetOfType`) keys are the same handle as the instantiation's, which no mapper changed. Chakra's `keyof Conditions` is one; `{ [K in keyof T]?: … }` and `{ [P in K]?: … }` are not, and each of those is listed. The check is one request per map that is listed and counted. The maps fixture (`Generic`) holds it: `Picked<Theirs, Keys>` before `Picked<Ours, Keys>`, the same 45 keys, and the project's fields are all listed.

157	### The checker's answer wins (ADR 0026, slice S4)
158	
159	The checker was an explicit opt-in until S8 made it the default (below). When it runs, its answer replaces the structural one prop by prop, at each surface:
160	
161	- **CLI.** `extract` waits for the checker: every candidate component in one program and one snapshot, as in slice 1. `--semantic-timeout-ms` (default 10,000) bounds the checker's start and each request; past it the run takes the structural result with one `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning that says it timed out. It bounds a hang, not the run: on 938 Chakra and MUI wrappers (`~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large`) the whole answer took 15 to 17 s with the `tsrs` process (its program 71 ms) and takes about 6 s with the built-in checker (S8), well within the default bound.
162	- **Addon and sessions.** As ADR 0022: the structural answer first, the checker's within `semanticWaitMs` (default 150), a late answer for the next request. The premise that the checker is too slow for a first story still holds with tsrs: Chakra's `Button` (about 1,100 props) takes a median 402 ms through the Rust client (see [gate measurements](gate-measurements.md#first-answer-s4)). Where the structural answer has no props (`Button` among them: the structural pass has props for 140 of the 938 wrappers of `gate-large`), the story waits up to `semanticWaitEmptyMs` (2,000 ms) instead, so its first answer is the checker's. The addon's `prefetchStories` (default 1) pays that wait before a browser asks: when `storybook dev` starts it asks Storybook's docgen service for the opening story's component, which starts the session and the checker and stores the answer where the browser reads it (see [gate measurements](gate-measurements.md#startup-prefetch-trail-332)).
163	- **A prop the checker could not read.** Where the checker's type of a prop holds an `opaque` part (an import or a name it did not resolve, a conditional type it left open, signatures it could not read) and the structural pass read the same prop's type in full, the prop keeps the structural type and its `degradedBy` also lists the checker's reasons: the checker did not confirm the type, so it is marked rather than silently trusted. One `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` `Info` diagnostic counts those props and names their components. A type the checker only cut at a limit (`truncated`) is still its answer, and so is an opaque checker type where the structural one is opaque too. On the 938 wrappers this applies to 60 props, such as Chakra's `cornerShape`, which the checker answers with its error type, and `storageManager`, whose `StorageManager` it left opaque.
164	- **Gate.** The construct suite's checker lane holds `checker-expectations.json` against `expectations.json`: no row may rank below the structural path unless it lists an `improvement` reason (`apps/oracle/construct-suite/README.md`, "The checker lane").

166	### Diagnostics a checker answer supersedes
167	
168	A diagnostic belongs to the pass that reported it and to the components in its `affects`. Once the checker answers for a component, a structural diagnostic about what that answer replaces no longer describes the component: the prefetch spike (PR 432) found Chakra's `Button` handed to React's docgen with the checker's 1,137 props in hand, because the structural "Cannot find the component 'Button'" warning stayed on the answer and the addon's `fallback: 'degraded'` reads any warning as incomplete props. Each code's decision is `DiagnosticCode::superseded_by_checker` (`crates/core/src/types/diagnostic.rs`, a match with no wildcard arm, so a new code needs one), and one function applies it for both merges, the whole-project one and a session's, in time, late or from the answer cache (`drop_superseded`, `crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs`). It takes the answered component out of the diagnostic's `affects`, and drops the diagnostic once it affects none: a diagnostic several components share stays for those the checker did not answer, and one that affects no component (a file's, the run's) is not touched. It runs before the checker's own diagnostics are added, so it never reads them.
169	
170	Superseded, so dropped once the checker answers, unless a structural prop the checker did not return still holds a part the structural pass could not read (the diagnostic names the component, not the prop, and may be about it):
171	
172	- `UNRESOLVABLE_IMPORT`: a component the structural pass could not find (`ComponentProps<typeof Button>` of a factory it does not model), an import or a type name it could not resolve, a builtin name it took as React's. The checker's answer has its own types for those props. It stays when a prop of the merged answer lists `unresolvableImport` in its `degradedBy`: the checker could not resolve a name either, which is the same fault in the project seen by both passes.
173	- `GENERIC_ARGUMENT_MISMATCH`: an unfilled type parameter left as a bare name in a structural prop type.
174	- `OPAQUE_TYPE`, `INDEXED_ACCESS_OPAQUE`, `TEMPLATE_LITERAL_OPAQUE`: a structural prop type left opaque or as a pattern. Where the checker could not read the type either, its own marker says so: the prop's `degradedBy`, and the `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` info for props that keep their structural type.
175	- `MAX_DEPTH_EXCEEDED`, `CIRCULAR_REFERENCE`: where the structural resolver stopped following a prop type.
176	
177	Not superseded, so they stay:
178	
179	- `JS_DOC_DEFAULT_MISMATCH`: default values stay structural.
180	- `DISCRIMINATED_UNION`: `discriminantProp` stays structural.
181	- `MISSING_TYPE_LIBRARY`: inheritance layers and curated inherited props stay structural.
182	- `IO_ERROR`, `PARSE_ERROR`, `EXCESSIVE_NESTING`, `SKIPPED_CANDIDATE`: about a file and what the extractor found in it, not a component's props.
183	- `COMPONENT_KEY_COLLISION`, `DUPLICATE_ENUM_NAME`: about the output's keys.
184	- `INTERNAL_PANIC`: a defect, whichever pass answers.
185	- `UNKNOWN`: reported by a consumer, not the structural pass.
186	- `SEMANTIC_BACKEND`: the checker's own: it is unavailable, it stopped, it has not answered yet, a component kept its structural result (an instantiation that did not form, a component that is not exported), an edit it was not told about, props it could not read.
187	
188	The addon decides `fallback: 'degraded'` from the warnings and errors left on the answer, which are now the structural ones that still stand and the checker's own.

190	### Generic components (ADR 0026, slice S5)
191	
192	A generic component's props parameter has its type parameters open: `function Poly<E extends ElementType = 'div'>(props: PolyProps<E>)` has two props (`as` typed `E`, and its own), where `<Poly />` has every attribute of a `div`. The API has no request that instantiates a signature, so `crates/semantic/src/instantiate.rs` writes the instantiation as source and lets the checker form it:
193	
194	- **Which instantiation.** The one `<Poly />` renders: the first type parameter's declared default, printed by the checker (`getTypeParametersOfSignature`, `getDefaultFromTypeParameter`, `typeToString`). The checker fills the parameters after it from their own defaults, which may refer to the first. A component whose first type parameter declares no default is unchanged: its props keep the open parameters, since no instantiation is the one a story renders.
195	- **How.** Once every file is answered, one file, `__caliper_instantiations__.ts` in the project root, declares one line per generic component, `import type { "Poly" as CaliperComponent0 } from "/abs/Poly.tsx"; export type CaliperProbe0 = Parameters<typeof CaliperComponent0<"div">>[0];`, and is added to a second snapshot of the same program through `createSnapshot`'s `fileSystem` layer (`{ "kind": "layer", "files": { path: text } }`), which both tsrs `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta` and the Go `7.1.0-beta` read and neither writes to disk. The props are those of `getDeclaredTypeOfSymbol(CaliperProbe0)`, read and converted as any props type is, in that snapshot.
196	- **Same type, not same name.** A printed default is text read in another module: `type FormData = { id: string }` in the component's module prints as `FormData`, which the probe file, with the default DOM libraries, resolves to the global `FormData` without an error. Each line also declares `CaliperSignature0 = typeof CaliperComponent0` and `CaliperArgument0_0 = <the printed default>`, and a component is read only when `getDeclaredTypeOfSymbol(CaliperArgument0_0)` is, in the probe's own snapshot, the type id of the default `getDefaultFromTypeParameter` gives for that signature (`arguments_keep_their_meaning`, the one place this is enforced). A default that is the same name for another type, or a type written anew (an inline object type), keeps the structural props: `the instantiation Form<FormData> could not be formed: a name in its type arguments means something else where the instantiation is written than in the component's module`.
197	- **When it cannot form.** The file's errors (`getSemanticDiagnostics`) are matched to components by line, and only errors in the probe file count: the response also holds errors the checker found in other files while forming the instantiations. A component whose line has an error keeps its structural props, and the fallback reason names the instantiation and the checker's message: `the instantiation Configured<Settings> could not be formed: Cannot find name 'Settings'.` (a default the checker prints by a name only the component's module sees). A props type that is a union after instantiation falls back as any union props type does. No props are read from an instantiation that did not form.
198	- **Cost.** Nothing for a component that is not generic: whether it is comes with the signature already fetched. A generic one costs three requests to find its default; a run with any costs one more snapshot (4 ms on the fixture, the first snapshot's parsed files reused), three requests for the file (its module, exports and errors) and its release, and one per component for the instantiation's type, then the props requests the component would cost anyway.
199	- **Gate.** `Poly<'div'>` has at least 260 props and `'a'` differs: 281 and 289 on both checkers (`crates/semantic/src/instantiate.rs`, `crates/semantic/tests/instantiate.rs`, against tsrs in the checker lane and the Go checker in Test / Rust). With the whole-project merge, `@types/react`'s props stay with the inheritance layers as for any component, so the CLI shows the component's own props, `as` as `'div'`.

201	### Watch (ADR 0026, slice S6)
202	
203	A warm checker keeps the snapshot it answered from, and the next request brings it up to date instead of building the program again (`crates/semantic/src/on_demand.rs`):
204	
205	- **Telling the checker.** Every change a `WatchSession` applies reaches its checker before any request that may read it: `update_file` and `ensure_fresh` pass the files they applied, a rebuild or a cold start passes "everything" (`SemanticProvider::changed`, `SourceChange`), in the same order as the requests, through the checker's queue.
206	- **Bringing the snapshot up to date.** `updateSnapshot` with `fileNotifications` (`changed` for a file on disk, `deleted` for one that is gone) and `ensurePrograms: true`; a request for another file also passes `reconfigurePrograms` with its root. Both checkers need `ensurePrograms`: without it a synthetic program keeps the old text even of a file it was told about, and with it the response lists the files whose text changed. Files not named are kept as parsed. A snapshot nothing changed is answered from as it is; an old one is released once its successor exists.
207	- **An edit nobody announced.** Neither checker sees an edit it is not told about (an update without the file in `fileNotifications` answers from the old text, and so does one told about another file), so before an answer the kept snapshot is checked: after each reply the files its program read are listed (`getSourceFileNames`, 1,855 for Chakra's `Button`) and stamped by modification time and length, and before the next answer they are stamped again (about 1.5 ms on four threads). A file that changed and was not announced makes the answer come from a fresh snapshot (`createSnapshot` reads everything from the disk), with a `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning that names the file. A file modified within 2 s of the snapshot's read cannot be told from a later edit by its stamp, so it is read again at every update until it settles: never a warning, never stale. A file that cannot be listed or stamped makes the next request build afresh.
208	- **Not seen.** A file created, without an announcement, where an import failed to resolve: it is not in the program, so it has no stamp. The session announces creations; only a writer that bypasses it is missed. A change to the tsconfig's compiler options still needs a new process, as before.
209	- **Memory.** Every request counts toward the 64 programs of a process, and the memory check is unchanged; a replaced process takes its snapshot with it. The built-in checker keeps one session and its snapshot for the whole watch session, bounded as under "On demand" above.

213	Where a prop is declared, its tags and the component's `composes` come from the checker's answer, not from the structural prop of the same name (`crates/semantic/src/declared.rs`, `Converter::composes`), so they no longer depend on the resolver S7 removes.

225	### Defaults and union order (ADR 0026, slice S7a2)
226	
227	The checker has no parameter initializer and returns a union's members sorted, so these two facts come from oxc's syntax, read from the files the checker's answer names (`crates/core/src/types/semantic/syntax.rs`), each file once per merge. One function decides each fact in the merge: `default_of` and `declared_order` (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs`).
228	
229	- **Default.** The component's code default for the prop, found by the extractor's own defaults code (`extractor/defaults.rs`, `defaultProps`) on the component's file, matched by display name and exports; else the checker's `@default` or `@defaultValue` tag; else the structural default. The code wins over the tag, as in react-docgen-typescript.
230	- **Union order.** The union the prop's declaration writes (`crates/core/src/extractor/written.rs`): the member of its `parent` interface in `parent.fileName`, or for a prop with no parent (a type literal), a type literal member of the component's file that is shown to be (part of) its props type: the body of the module-level alias the component's declaration names (or a member of the intersection or union that body is), or a type literal written in the component's declaration outside any body. A type literal elsewhere in the file (an imported props type with a local look-alike) says nothing. A same-file non-generic alias or enum it names is flattened in place, only where it is the declaration in scope: a type parameter, or a type an enclosing namespace, function or block declares, shadows it and the name stays as written. Each alias is flattened once per file, in the module scope, a member stated twice counts once, and a union stating more than 1,024 members through its aliases is not read (a `MAX_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` info diagnostic names the file). A member is matched by what it states (a literal, a keyword, a name it answers to), or by its kind when the written union has one member of that kind (a function, an object literal, an intersection, a template). Where it places every member, its order is used. Where it places some, the structural union's order is used if the structural union placed any member (even when that order is the checker's own), else the placed members come first in written order and the rest follow in the checker's order. Only the top-level union is ordered; a union nested in an object, array or function keeps the structural order where there is one.
231	- **What oxc alone cannot see.** A union whose members come through an import (`xChannel?: ColorChannel`, `Placement`): following it needs module resolution, which the resolver or the checker has, so the members stay in the checker's order (by kind, then value: not alphabetical, and not marked).
