docs/STATUS.md:30:## Known gaps of the structural resolver (the fallback, and `--no-checker`)
docs/STATUS.md:34:**The TypeScript checker is the default** (ADR 0026, S8 done 2026-11-12). `extract`, `check` and `inspect` merge the built-in checker's answer (the `tsrs` crates, the only checker since trail 369 slice 4 removed `--tsc-path`) over the structural one prop by prop, napi sessions and the Storybook addon ask it per component within `semanticWaitMs` (ADR 0022), and `--no-checker` (`checker: false`) turns it off; `watch` and the Vite plugin stay structural. A prop the checker could not read keeps the structural type with `degradedBy`, and a checker that fails to start or times out falls back to the structural result with one warning. The gates before the flip (checker lane, determinism, Linux CI, memory past 600 edits, tsrs-against-Go parity) are recorded in ADR 0026. It began as the opt-in slice 1 (ADR 0006, ADR 0007, `type-checker-integration.md`), whose accuracy was verified against real RDT: 0 missing/extra props on 13 hand-picked components, and on `7.1.0-beta` against the full 44-file fixture corpus (5,508/5,522 `required` matches, 5,266/5,522 type-string matches). TypeScript 7.1's Go checker also runs, test-only, as an oracle for structural prop types (`docs/measurement.md`); the weekly record measures the checker, the default (`oracle.universe_version` 5).
docs/rdt-differences.md:18:- **not judged**: the oracle did not evaluate the checker's type, so nothing was compared (`docs/measurement.md`, `oracle.universe_version` 4). The measurements below were taken before it existed and counted such props as identical.
docs/rdt-differences.md:32:The last column is `oracle.tools.rdt.wrong_listed`: the share of the props RDT lists that the checker contradicts. It is over every function the checker takes for a component, as the record was until `universe_version` 2 (2026-11-10); a later record has it over candidate components only (`oracle.tools`) and over every function in `oracle.tools_all_functions`, and its spectrum row has more shared props, because default exports are named (`docs/measurement.md`). react-docgen throws on 51 of 295 antd files and 265 of 1,240 shadcn files (17% and 21%) and so omits their props.
docs/rdt-differences.md:114:**Measured.** `wrong`, counted: 2 props (react-hook-form's `watch` and `getValues`). The comparator scored it right.
docs/rdt-differences.md:320:**What differs.** With `--html-attributes full` Caliper lists React's DOM attributes. For `React.ComponentProps<'button'> & { variant?: 'solid' | 'ghost' }` it lists 290 props, RDT lists the same 290, and the oracle's universe is 1 (`variant`), because it excludes `@types/react`.
docs/rdt-differences.md:324:**Measured.** Not measured. The oracle never scores a prop outside its universe, so Caliper-only counts do not appear in any column, and a count of "Caliper-only props" taken from the JSON is inflated by colliding keys and should not be quoted.
docs/gate-measurements.md:64:- **Loud failure.** `crates/semantic/tests/watch.rs` edits a file the component imports without telling the checker: the answer carries one `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning naming that file and has the new prop (read from a fresh snapshot). With the comparison disabled the same test fails (no warning, the old prop). It runs on tsrs in the checker lane and on the Go checker in Test / Rust; `crates/core/tests/semantic_hook.rs` holds that `update_file`, `ensure_fresh` and a rebuild each tell the checker.
docs/gate-measurements.md:84:- **A session's kept answers** (the Storybook addon's configuration through the native binding: lazy, dependencies loaded, nothing collapsed, `semanticWaitMs` and `semanticWaitEmptyMs` 60 s so every answer is the checker's; `gate-large`'s components asked one at a time, the process's RSS read every 100). Each checker answer is kept for the next request, and each held its own copy of every prop: 1,257, 1,930 and 2,602 MiB after 100, 200 and 300 components, about 6.7 MiB per Chakra component (trail 369 slice 2 read 5,365 MiB at 900). With the checker on by default a session that asked for every story would run out of memory, so the answer cache now shares one copy of each equal prop per generation (`AnswerCache::shared` in `crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`), as the whole-project merge does: 716, 786 and 825 MiB at 100, 200 and 300, **1,007 MiB after all 938, peak 1,058 MiB**. The structural session alone (`checker: false`) peaks at 377 MiB.
docs/gate-measurements.md:105:- **How it reaches Storybook.** Storybook 11 starts its docgen worker on the first `extractDocgen` (`createDocgenWorkerClient`: `worker ??= new DocgenWorker`), so nothing in the worker runs earlier. The addon's preset adds an `experimental_devServer` hook, which Storybook applies before the builders start; after Storybook's own hook registers the `core/docgen` service, it reads the story index and calls `getService('core/docgen', { internal: true }).commands.extractDocgen({ id })` (`storybook/internal/core-server`, internal API, Storybook `11.0.0-alpha.9`) for the opening story's component. The command runs the provider chain and writes the answer to the service's state, which the manager receives with its first sync. The manager's Controls panel subscribes once the story is prepared; that subscription's load calls `extractDocgen` again, so the provider is asked a second time and answers from the session, but `isInitialLoading` is false while the stored payload is there, so the panel shows it at once.
docs/gate-measurements.md:106:- **Harness.** `~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/prefetch`: `storybook dev` (11.0.0-alpha.9, Vite 8, `@storybook/builder-vite` 10.6.2 from the pnpm store with its mock extraction stubbed, since the store has no 11 builder) over 40 stories of `gate-large`'s Chakra wrappers with a `ChakraProvider` decorator, `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'` on the pinned tsrs and `fallback: 'never'`. Playwright opens the root URL as soon as `index.json` answers, as `storybook dev` opens the browser once the index is built. The browser's request and answer times are the manager's websocket frames (`services:command-invoke` for `extractDocgen`, the `core/docgen` state entry); a provider registered after the addon's logs each request in the worker. Shared machine at load 20 to 160; 13 runs with the prefetch (9 of one story, 4 of three) and 9 without, interleaved.
docs/gate-measurements.md:111:- **Found on the way.** Storybook hands a preset its own options merged with the addon's; its own `cache` (a file-system cache object) reached the native session as the addon's `cache`, which it refused, so the addon could not start in any real `storybook dev` until the preset dropped a non-boolean `cache`. And with the default `fallback: 'degraded'`, `ChakraButton` is handed to React's docgen even when the checker answers, because the structural warning that `Button` was not found stays on the answer.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:3:**Status:** the checker is the default ([ADR 0026](adr/0026-the-checker-is-the-type-authority.md) S8, see "The checker is the default" below): `extract`, `check`, `inspect`, napi sessions and the Storybook addon ask it, and `--no-checker` (`checker: false`) turns it off. It began as an opt-in second resolver ([ADR 0006](adr/0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md), [ADR 0007](adr/0007-backend-discovers-components-and-compiles-in.md), "Slice 1" below); its answer wins prop by prop (see "The checker's answer wins"). The checker is built in (the `tsrs` crates, see "The checker"); there is no other. Structural extraction is the fallback, and what `--no-checker`, `watch` and the Vite plugin run. Separately, TypeScript 7.1's checker runs as a test-only oracle for structural prop types (`scripts/weekly.py --oracle`, `docs/measurement.md`). **Last verified:** 2026-10-23 for slice 1 against `7.1.0-beta`; 2026-09-27 for the Cost measurements, each naming its nightly; 2026-10-22 for the API table against the `7.1.0-beta` package; 2026-10-23 for the fixture-corpus parity on `7.1.0-beta`.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:70:- **Provenance:** `Info` diagnostics with code `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` whose `affects` lists the output keys: one for the components the checker resolved, one per fallback reason. A first-class per-component field would change the canonical JSON and needs a `SCHEMA_VERSION` bump (`crates/core/src/types/output.rs`).
docs/type-checker-integration.md:71:- **Fallback:** a checker that cannot start or does not answer in time gives the structural result plus one `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning, never an error. Per component, the structural result stands for: not exported, class or non-function, overloaded, no props parameter, `any`/`unknown`/union props type, a generic component whose instantiation at its default could not be formed (see "Generic components"), none of the exports the extractor recorded for it found (or found declared in another file), a generic sub-component reached through its parent's property, or a request the checker rejected. Each is listed with its reason.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:72:- **Which export:** the extractor records how the module exports each component (ADR 0027): its export names (`default` included), or for a sub-component attached to an exported one the path through that export (`Menu.Item = Item` beside `export default Menu` is `default.Item`). The checker asks for exactly those, follows an alias to what it aliases, reads an attached sub-component as the property of its parent's type, and checks that the declaration is in the component's file. It never takes the module's `default` unless `default` is a recorded export, and never looks a component up by its display name. Each request carries the component's output key, its answer or fallback carries it back, and the merge (whole-project and session, in time or late) finds the entry by that key alone.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:168:A diagnostic belongs to the pass that reported it and to the components in its `affects`. Once the checker answers for a component, a structural diagnostic about what that answer replaces no longer describes the component: the prefetch spike (PR 432) found Chakra's `Button` handed to React's docgen with the checker's 1,137 props in hand, because the structural "Cannot find the component 'Button'" warning stayed on the answer and the addon's `fallback: 'degraded'` reads any warning as incomplete props. Each code's decision is `DiagnosticCode::superseded_by_checker` (`crates/core/src/types/diagnostic.rs`, a match with no wildcard arm, so a new code needs one), and one function applies it for both merges, the whole-project one and a session's, in time, late or from the answer cache (`drop_superseded`, `crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs`). It takes the answered component out of the diagnostic's `affects`, and drops the diagnostic once it affects none: a diagnostic several components share stays for those the checker did not answer, and one that affects no component (a file's, the run's) is not touched. It runs before the checker's own diagnostics are added, so it never reads them.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:188:The addon decides `fallback: 'degraded'` from the warnings and errors left on the answer, which are now the structural ones that still stand and the checker's own.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:197:- **When it cannot form.** The file's errors (`getSemanticDiagnostics`) are matched to components by line, and only errors in the probe file count: the response also holds errors the checker found in other files while forming the instantiations. A component whose line has an error keeps its structural props, and the fallback reason names the instantiation and the checker's message: `the instantiation Configured<Settings> could not be formed: Cannot find name 'Settings'.` (a default the checker prints by a name only the component's module sees). A props type that is a union after instantiation falls back as any union props type does. No props are read from an instantiation that did not form.
docs/type-checker-integration.md:231:- **What oxc alone cannot see.** A union whose members come through an import (`xChannel?: ColorChannel`, `Placement`): following it needs module resolution, which the resolver or the checker has, so the members stay in the checker's order (by kind, then value: not alphabetical, and not marked). A type literal declared in another file than the component's (it has no `parent` to find it by). A `@default` on a prop mapped through `Omit` or `Pick` of an instantiated generic (Spectrum's `Popover` `placement`): the checker gives it no declaration, so no tags. Code defaults the extractor does not read: `defaultProps` assigned in another module or from a variable, spread or computed defaults, and defaults applied inside a hook (`mergeProps`).
docs/type-checker-integration.md:327:- **Cold path only.** The hook is synchronous and runs on the cold path; `WatchSession::update_file` does not run it.

1	// The construct suite through the checker path (ADR 0026): `caliper-docgen extract` (the checker is on by default) over
2	// apps/oracle/construct-suite, and each row's verdict against its golden. It is a gate on
3	// construct-suite/checker-expectations.json: it prints the report, then exits 1 when a row is better or worse than the
4	// expectation allows (an improvement means the gap closed: update the file), when the checker did not answer for a row,
5	// when the checker backend was unavailable, or when checker-expectations.json ranks a row below expectations.json
6	// without an `improvement` reason (ADR 0026's S4 gate). Run it with `just test-checker-lane`, or by hand:
7	//
8	//   cargo build --release -p caliper-docgen
9	//   CALIPER_SEMANTIC=1 pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:checker
10	//
11	// A row the checker did not answer for (it kept the structural result) is listed apart: its verdict says nothing about
12	// the checker. `--json <file>` also writes every row with the type each side gave.
13	import { existsSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
14	import { join, resolve } from 'node:path'
15	import {
16	  againstStructural,
17	  checkerExpectations,
18	  dependsOnFallback,
19	  fallbackWorklist,
20	  laneFailures,
21	  runCheckerLane,
22	  structuralExpectations,
23	  type Row,
24	} from './construct-checker-run.ts'
25	import { isAgreement } from './vocabulary.ts'
26	
27	if (process.env.CALIPER_SEMANTIC !== '1') {
28	  console.error('construct-checker-lane: set CALIPER_SEMANTIC=1 to run the suite through the checker.')
29	  process.exit(2)
30	}
31	const bin = resolve(
32	  process.env.CALIPER_BIN ?? join(import.meta.dirname, '..', '..', '..', 'target', 'release', 'caliper-docgen'),
33	)
34	if (!existsSync(bin)) {
35	  console.error(`construct-checker-lane: no caliper binary at ${bin}; build one or set CALIPER_BIN.`)
36	  process.exit(2)
37	}
38	const jsonOut = process.argv.includes('--json') ? process.argv[process.argv.indexOf('--json') + 1] : undefined
39	
40	const run = runCheckerLane(bin)
41	if (run.backendProblem !== undefined) {
42	  console.error(`construct-checker-lane: the checker was unavailable: ${run.backendProblem}`)
43	  process.exit(1)
44	}
45	const { elapsedMs, rows } = run
46	
47	const checkerRows = rows.filter((row) => row.answered)
48	const structuralRows = rows.filter((row) => !row.answered)
49	const green = (row: Row) => isAgreement(row.verdict)
50	console.log(
51	  `checker path over ${rows.length} rows in ${elapsedMs} ms: ${checkerRows.length} answered by the checker, ${structuralRows.length} kept their structural result`,
52	)
53	const count = (list: Row[]) => {
54	  const tally = new Map<string, number>()
55	  for (const row of list) tally.set(row.verdict, (tally.get(row.verdict) ?? 0) + 1)
56	  return [...tally].map(([verdict, n]) => `${verdict} ${n}`).join(', ')
57	}
58	console.log(`  checker rows: ${count(checkerRows)}`)
59	console.log('')
60	console.log('Rows the checker answered that are not identical or spelled (verdict | structural expectation | golden):')

lines: - **Default.** The component's code default for the prop, found by the extractor's own defaults code (`extractor/defaults.rs`, `defaultProps`) on the component's file, matched by display name and exports; else the checker's `@default` or `@defaultValue` tag; else the structural default. The code wins over the tag, as in react-docgen-typescript.

- **Union order.** The union the prop's declaration writes (`crates/core/src/extractor/written.rs`): the member of its `parent` interface in `parent.fileName`, or for a prop with no parent (a type literal), a type literal member of the component's file that is shown to be (part of) its props type: the body of the module-level alias the component's declaration names (or a member of the intersection or union that body is), or a type literal written in the component's declaration outside any body. A type literal elsewhere in the file (an imported props type with a local look-alike) says nothing. A same-file non-generic alias or enum it names is flattened in place, only where it is the declaration in scope: a type parameter, or a type an enclosing namespace, function or block declares, shadows it and the name stays as written. Each alias is flattened once per file, in the module scope, a member stated twice counts once, and a union stating more than 1,024 members through its aliases is not read (a `MAX_DEPTH_EXCEEDED` info diagnostic names the file). A member is matched by what it states (a literal, a keyword, a name it answers to), or by its kind when the written union has one member of that kind (a function, an object literal, an intersection, a template). Where it places every member, its order is used. Where it places some, the structural union's order is used if the structural union placed any member (even when that order is the checker's own), else the placed members come first in written order and the rest follow in the checker's order. Only the top-level union is ordered; a union nested in an object, array or function keeps the structural order where there is one.

- **What oxc alone cannot see.** A union whose members come through an import (`xChannel?: ColorChannel`, `Placement`): following it needs module resolution, which the resolver or the checker has, so the members stay in the checker's order (by kind, then value: not alphabetical, and not marked). A type literal declared in another file than the component's (it has no `parent` to find it by). A `@default` on a prop mapped through `Omit` or `Pick` of an instantiated generic (Spectrum's `Popover` `placement`): the checker gives it no declaration, so no tags. Code defaults the extractor does not read: `defaultProps` assigned in another module or from a variable, spread or computed defaults, and defaults applied inside a hook (`mergeProps`).

-- **Switch.** `extract --no-resolver-facts` (hidden, test-only; `ResolverFacts::Off`) makes the merge take neither fact from the structural answer; the construct suite's checker lane runs with it. S7b extends it to the other facts.

+- **Switch.** `extract --no-resolver-facts` (hidden, test-only; `ResolverFacts::Off`) makes the merge take neither fact from the structural answer; the construct suite's checker lane runs with it. S7b extended it to the whole fallback (below).

- **Measured** (`extract` with the checker, then behind `--experimental-semantic-types`, with the weekly's options, tsrs `0.23.0-ts7.1.0-beta`, against the run before this slice). Before, the structural answer gave the order of 2,736 of Spectrum's 3,194 merged union props and 187 of gate-large's 432,813, and every default: on Spectrum 870 from code, 378 `@default` tags the checker also gives, 15 from the resolver only; on gate-large 499 tags. Now, Spectrum: 27 props gain a code default and none loses one; 11 of 3,686 unions change order, each to the written one (`focusMode?: 'child' | 'cell'`, `slot?: string | null`). With `--no-resolver-facts` 15 defaults (the mapped `@default` case above) and 22 more union orders (imported aliases) differ. gate-large: 834 props gain a default (the checker's `@default` tags of props only the checker returns) and none loses one; 1,452 of 432,690 unions take the written order (`translate?: 'yes' | 'no'`, `css`); with `--no-resolver-facts` no default and 16 more union orders differ (members through an import, such as MUI's `timeout?: TransitionProps['timeout'] | 'auto'`).

- **Cost.** Reading and parsing the files: 0.8 to 1.0 ms of Chakra's `Button` first answer (about 470 ms), whose union props are declared in 83 KB of Chakra's `system.gen.d.ts` and @types/react's 183 KB `index.d.ts`. On gate-large, peak RSS 610 to 616 MB against 608 to 612, and the same CPU time (two runs each).

- **Gate.** Both lanes compare `default` and member order on every row; the checker lane runs with `--no-resolver-facts` and passes every row. Rows `objects/41` to `43` (a destructured default, `defaultProps`, a code default over a different `@default`) and `literals/35` (a type literal's union) cover what a single-file row can; a union through an import needs the cross-file rows of S7b.

# Deterministic construct suite

One small fixture per type construct, each compared with what TypeScript's checker says. Unlike the weekly oracle (`scripts/weekly.py --oracle`), it runs on a handful of files in seconds, needs no corpus, and fails on any change in how Caliper reads a construct.

## Layout

```
construct-suite/
  tsconfig.json              the options the checker reads the fixtures with
  expectations.json          row id -> allowed verdicts (and the reason for each gap)
  <family>/<NN>-<slug>.tsx   a fixture
  <family>/<NN>-<slug>.golden.json   its committed golden, written by construct:capture
  <family>/<NN>-<slug>.<Component>.golden.json   the golden of each component of a fixture that lists several
```

A row id is `<family>/<NN>-<slug>`, or `<family>/<NN>-<slug>#<Component>` for a component of a fixture that lists several. The harness is `../src/construct-suite.ts` (pure helpers), `../src/construct-capture.ts` (the capture script) and `../tests/construct-suite.test.ts`. `seed/` holds the three rows that prove the harness. The other families are `literals`, `objects`, `tuples-arrays`, `utility-mapped`, `generics`, `react` and `exports`.

A fixture declares one `interface Props` with one prop `p`, and exports a component `Row` that takes it:

The harness is `../src/construct-suite.ts` (pure helpers), `../src/construct-capture.ts` (the capture script) and `../tests/construct-suite.test.ts`. `seed/` holds the three rows that prove the harness. The lane and `tests/construct-checker-lane.test.ts` (which needs no binary, so it runs with the package tests) hold the two files to it: a row whose checker verdicts rank below its `expectations.json` verdicts fails unless its `checker-expectations.json` entry gives an `"improvement"` reason, the case where the comparison scores the checker's answer lower although it states more (no row needs one today: `react/34` did until the comparator read `Omit<HTMLAttributes<…>>` as one family). An `"improvement"` on a row that does not rank below the structural path fails too, so the list stays honest. With `--experimental-semantic-types` or `semanticTypes: 'on-demand'`, a prop the TypeScript checker answers for takes its default and the order of its union's members from the source itself: the default the component's code gives it (a destructured parameter's initializer, `defaultProps`), else its `@default` tag, and the members in the order its declaration writes them. Props only the checker returns now have both too (938 Chakra and MUI wrappers: 834 more defaults, 1,452 unions in written order), and a few unions Caliper's own pass ordered wrong are fixed (`slot?: string | null`). Members that come through an imported type keep Caliper's own order, as before. For library users: `merge_semantic_with` takes a `ResolverFacts`, `MergedProps` has `diagnostics` and is no longer `Copy`, `apply_semantic_props` is gone (`merge_semantic` does what it did), and the merge functions read the source files the answer names.
